In mathematics, especially in [[differential topology]], '''Thom's second isotopy lemma''' is a family version of [[Thom's first isotopy lemma]]; i.e., it states a family of maps between [[Whitney stratified spaces]] is locally trivial when it is a '''Thom mapping'''.<ref name="statement">{{harvnb|Mather|2012|loc=Proposition 11.2.}}</ref> Like the first isotopy lemma, the lemma was introduced by [[René Thom]].

{{harv|Mather|2012|loc=§ 11}} gives a sketch of the proof. {{harv|Verona|1984}} gives a simplified proof. Like the first isotopy lemma, the lemma also holds for the stratification with [[Bekka's condition (C)]], which is weaker than Whitney's condition (B).<ref>§ 3 of {{cite book |last1=Bekka |first1=K. |chapter=C-Régularité et trivialité topologique |title=Singularity Theory and its Applications |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |date=1991 |volume=1462 |pages=42–62 |doi=10.1007/BFb0086373 |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/BFb0086373 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-540-53737-3 |language=en}}</ref>

==Thom mapping==

Let <math>f : M \to N</math> be a smooth map between smooth manifolds and <math>X, Y \subset M</math> submanifolds such that <math>f|_X, f|_Y</math> both have differential of constant rank. Then '''Thom's condition <math>(a_f)</math>''' is said to hold if for each sequence <math>x_i</math> in ''X'' converging to a point ''y'' in ''Y'' and such that <math>\operatorname{ker}(d(f|_{X})_{x_i})</math> converging to a plane <math>\tau</math> in the [[Grassmannian]], we have <math>\operatorname{ker}(d(f|_Y)_y) \subset \tau.</math><ref name="eleven">{{harvnb|Mather|2012|loc=§ 11.}}</ref>

Let <math>S \subset M, S' \subset N</math> be [[Whitney stratification|Whitney stratified]] closed subsets and <math>p : S \to Z, q : S' \to Z</math> maps to some smooth manifold ''Z'' such that <math>f : S \to S'</math> is a map over ''Z''; i.e., <math>f(S) \subset S'</math> and <math>q \circ f|_S = p</math>. Then <math>f</math> is called a '''Thom mapping''' if the following conditions hold:<ref name="eleven" /><!-- we really need to add a diagram. -->
*<math>f|_S, q</math> are proper.
*<math>q</math> is a submersion on each stratum of <math>S'</math>.
*For each stratum ''X'' of ''S'', <math>f(X)</math> lies in a stratum ''Y'' of <math>S'</math> and <math>f : X \to Y</math> is a submersion.
*Thom's condition <math>(a_f)</math> holds for each pair of strata of <math>S</math>.

Then Thom's second isotopy lemma says that a Thom mapping is locally trivial over ''Z''; i.e., each point ''z'' of ''Z'' has a neighborhood ''U'' with homeomorphisms <math>h_1 : p^{-1}(z) \times U \to p^{-1}(U), h_2 : q^{-1}(z) \times U \to q^{-1}(U)</math> over ''U'' such that <math>f \circ h_1 = h_2 \circ (f|_{p^{-1}(z)} \times \operatorname{id})</math>.<ref name="eleven" />
